items.summary: Choose Default or Classic in Settings > Control Scheme and learn the Xbox buttons that matter most before anything else.
instructions: Pause, choose Settings. Tabs run Control Scheme, Controller, Gameplay, Display, UI, Camera, Audio; switch tabs with LB/RB.
On Control Scheme pick Default, Classic or Left-Handed. Left-Handed swaps the sticks and shoulder buttons.
Default (on foot): click Left Stick to run, click again to sprint; A jump/climb; B crouch; X melee.
Classic moves these: A run, X jump, click Left Stick crouch, B melee. As a GTA V veteran you may prefer it.
Core Xbox Default buttons: LT aim (hold), RT shoot, RB cover, LB tap = holster / hold = loadout wheel, Y interact, View = map.
D-pad: Up = phone (hold = WAiNK), Left = radio, Right = explosives / partner menu, Down = objective, minimap, quick navigation.
In vehicles: RT accelerate, LT brake/reverse, A handbrake, click Left Stick = horn/nitrous.
Read the diagrams on the Control Scheme tab (On Foot, Aiming, Melee, Land/Water Vehicles, Aircraft, Bicycle, Swimming, Parachute).
Backing out of Settings asks SAVE SETTINGS?; confirm or your change is lost.

drills.name: Button walk-through
drills.setup: Any quiet street near Jason's house, on foot.
drills.howTo: Run, sprint, jump, crouch, take cover, open the loadout wheel, the phone and the map, saying each button out loud.

drills.name: Scheme A/B test
drills.setup: Try Default for one session and Classic for the next.
drills.howTo: Note which one you mis-press less during a short police chase. Keep it and stop switching.

items.goal: Do every core action (sprint, jump, crouch, cover, holster, loadout, phone, map, handbrake) without looking at the controller, 10 out of 10 times.

recommendedSettings.value: Default (or Classic if GTA V muscle memory keeps fighting you)
recommendedSettings.why: Classic puts run on A and crouch on the stick click, like older GTA layouts; Default is what every guide's button list uses.

items.notes: Button names are from G2A's Xbox Default list and The Games Wiki. PS5 guides map LT=L2, RT=R2, LB=L1, RB=R1, A=Cross, B=Circle, X=Square, Y=Triangle, View=touchpad. Adaptive triggers and the Adaptive Speed Limiter are PS5-only. Drills and goal are coaching suggestions built on the sourced mechanics, not taken from a guide.

items.summary: Set Targeting, Aim Assist Strength and the combat assists in Settings > Gameplay > Combat before you tune sensitivity.
instructions: Open Settings > Gameplay. The Combat group holds Targeting, Aim Assist Strength, Shooting Assist, Drive-By Assist, Quick Draw, Cover Selection and Holster in Vehicle.
Targeting: Lock-On (always tries to lock the nearest target), Partial (default: aim moves toward a nearby target but does not lock) or Free Aim.
Aim Assist Strength (0-5, default 4) slows the reticle as it passes over a target.
Shooting Assist helps track close targets on foot; Drive-By Assist aims at nearby targets when you shoot from a vehicle.
Quick Draw re-equips your last gun (the off-hand longarm if you carry two).
Holster in Vehicle: Automatic stows a drawn gun after a calm spell in a car; Manual leaves it to you.
games.gg's advice: choose Targeting first, then tune sensitivity around it.

drills.name: Partial vs Free Aim range test
drills.setup: Rodgers Ranch Market Range, Beginner class (free, pistol).
drills.howTo: Run the class 5 times on Partial, then 5 on Free Aim; write down your best time for each.

drills.name: Assist step-down
drills.setup: Same range, once Market Range Beginner Gold is easy.
drills.howTo: Drop Aim Assist Strength one step (4 to 3) and re-run until you are back to Gold.

items.goal: Gold (3 seconds or less) on Market Range Beginner with Targeting on Partial, 3 runs in a row.

recommendedSettings.why: Default, and what Beebom and G2A recommend: it pulls toward targets without taking control away like Lock-On.
Beebom keeps 4; lower it only once your aim is consistent.
Helps close-range tracking on foot.
Makes car shooting much easier while learning.
Faster to get back to your last gun.
One less thing in chases; switch to Manual if it stows your gun at bad moments.

items.notes: The Games Wiki says there is no lock-on, but the Targeting setting lists a Lock-On option (NerdsChalk, AllThingsHow, GTA6Map.net), so treat Lock-On as an assist mode, not a GTA V hard lock. Lock-On Time (Beebom: 4) appears only in Beebom. Drills and goal are coaching suggestions built on the sourced mechanics, not taken from a guide.

items.summary: Tune the four sensitivities, the two accelerations and the Aim Response Curve in Settings > Controller, one change at a time.
instructions: Open Settings > Controller. All four sensitivities (Horizontal/Vertical Look, Horizontal/Vertical Aim) and Look/Aim Acceleration start at 7 (Vice Manual reads Horizontal Look as 6; check yours).
Look Sensitivity = how fast the camera turns with the right stick. Aim Sensitivity = the same while holding LT.
Set Look first: raise Horizontal Look until a 180-degree turn feels quick but you do not overshoot doors.
Set Aim a little below Look (G2A), so fine aiming is calmer than general looking.
Leave both accelerations and the curve at default on the first pass (games.gg); then try lower Aim Acceleration if the reticle 'jumps'.
Aim Response Curve options: Standard, Linear, Precision, Aggressive. Linear or Precision give the most predictable small adjustments.
After every change, test on the same range drill before changing anything else.

drills.name: Overshoot test
drills.setup: Rodgers Ranch Market Range, Beginner class.
drills.howTo: Flick between the outermost targets; if you overshoot, drop Horizontal Aim by 1; if you are slow, raise it by 1.

drills.name: Tracking test
drills.setup: Hunting Range Beginner (free, pistol) at Rodgers Ranch.
drills.howTo: Track moving animals and go for heads; keep the value that gives the higher score.

items.goal: Settle on values that get you Gold (2,500 points) on Hunting Range Beginner, then do not change them for a week.

recommendedSettings.why: A bit faster than default for turning; games.gg suggests trying 9.
All three guides land on about 7.
Guides split; start in the middle and adjust with the overshoot test.
Lower vertical aim keeps headshots steady.
Leave at default first.
Lower acceleration ramps the reticle up less suddenly.
Linear gives a 1:1 feel; try Precision if small corrections feel too fast.

items.notes: The three guides disagree on exact numbers, so these are starting ranges, not one correct setting. Middle-of-range starting values (e.g. Horizontal Aim 6) are a coaching choice. Aircraft inversion is a separate setting (Inverted Controls > Aircraft Movement). Drills and goal are coaching suggestions built on the sourced mechanics, not taken from a guide.

items.summary: Lower the stick deadzones until just before drift, and change only one setting at a time.
instructions: Open Settings > Controller and find the left and right stick deadzone rows; Beebom gives the default as 4.
Drift test: lower a deadzone by one step, let go of the stick and watch the camera or character for 10 seconds.
If anything moves on its own, go back up one step. That is your lowest safe value (G2A: lowest value with no drift).
Change one setting at a time, then test it on the same drill (G2A).
Give a new value at least one full session before judging it; your hands need time to adapt.
Write your final values down so you can restore them after RESTORE DEFAULT or on a new console.

drills.name: Drift test
drills.setup: Stand still in an open area, then sit still in a parked car.
drills.howTo: Lower the right-stick deadzone one step at a time and watch for drift with hands off; repeat for the left stick.

drills.name: One-change log
drills.setup: A notes app on your real phone.
drills.howTo: Each session, change one setting, run the same range drill and note your result.

items.goal: Both deadzones at the lowest value with zero drift over a 10-second hands-off test, and a written list of your final settings.

recommendedSettings.value: 2-3 (Beebom; default 4), or lowest with no drift
recommendedSettings.why: Smaller deadzone = quicker response to small stick movements.

recommendedSettings.value: 2-3 (Beebom; default 4), or lowest with no drift
recommendedSettings.why: Finer aim adjustments; worn sticks may need more.

items.summary: Raise camera height for a wider view, slow the driver camera's snap-back, and turn off Weapon Sway for steadier aim.
instructions: Open Settings > Camera.
There is no field-of-view slider and no first-person mode; Height (On Foot) and Height (All Vehicles) (Low/Medium/High) are the closest thing. High shows more.
Horizontal/Vertical Follow Speed (default 10) set how fast the camera swings back behind you; Follow Delay (Driver) sets how long it waits.
Hold D-pad Down for camera options, including three camera distances and the Cinematic camera.
Comfort: Weapon Sway (On by default) sways your gun while aiming; Off holds aim steady. Camera Shake and Camera Bob cut shake on runs and crashes.
Cinematic Kill Shot Frequency and Cinematic Vehicle Crash Frequency (default 3) control slow-motion cut-aways; lower them to keep control.
Aircraft: Follow Roll rolls the camera with the plane; Off keeps the horizon steadier.
Phone Display: Default or First Person (the only first-person view in the game).

drills.name: Height comparison lap
drills.setup: Gellhorn Raceway, Introduction race, or your own block.
drills.howTo: One lap at Medium, one at High camera height; keep the one where you clip fewer corners.

drills.name: Sway on/off range test
drills.setup: Rodgers Ranch Market Range.
drills.howTo: Five runs with Weapon Sway On, five Off; compare best times.

items.goal: Finish 3 clean laps of a Gellhorn Raceway loop with your chosen camera, never losing sight of the road after a corner.

recommendedSettings.why: Widest view available, since there is no FOV slider (Vice Manual, Output Lag).
See more traffic ahead; applies to aircraft too.
Holds your aim steady (GTA6Map.net).
Less shake in chases and crashes.

recommendedSettings.value: Raise from 0 if the camera snaps back too soon after you look around
recommendedSettings.why: Per GTA6Map.net.

recommendedSettings.setting: Cinematic Kill Shot Frequency / Cinematic Vehicle Crash Frequency
recommendedSettings.why: Fewer cut-aways in fights and chases.
Steadier horizon while flying.

items.notes: The High/Off picks are coaching choices based on what the guides say each option does; no guide gives one best camera preset. A launch glitch can force first person (Output Lag), but it is not a setting. Drills and goal are coaching suggestions built on the sourced mechanics, not taken from a guide.

items.summary: Make the minimap and compass always visible and keep the combat indicators on so you never miss a threat.
instructions: Open Settings > UI (70 rows in 11 groups).
Navigation: Minimap = On / Dynamic (default) / Off; Minimap Size = Default / Large; Compass = On / Dynamic / Off (default Off).
GPS Route (On) draws your route; GPS Turn Indicators = On / Highways / Off shows upcoming turns on the HUD.
Reticle: Persistent Center Dot keeps a dot in the middle of the screen; Reticle Size and Reticle Shape make the crosshair bigger or simpler.
Combat: keep Threat Indicators (markers for nearby threats) and Damage Region Highlights On.
HUD Notifications: Reminder Tips give help after you fail, get busted or are wanted.
Map Blip Size, Minimap Blip Size and In-World Marker Size can be set to large.

drills.name: Minimap glance habit
drills.setup: Free roam; start a 1-star chase on purpose.
drills.howTo: Glance at the minimap/compass every few seconds to read the police search area, then break away.

drills.name: Turn-indicator drive
drills.setup: Set a waypoint across Vice City.
drills.howTo: Drive there using only GPS Turn Indicators and the minimap; no stopping to open the map.

items.goal: Reach 3 waypoints across Vice City in a row without opening the pause map.

recommendedSettings.why: Always visible instead of only on demand (Dynamic).
Dynamic shows it while driving, wanted or on a D-pad press.
Easier to read the route and search area at a glance.
Directions on all roads while driving.
Shows threats nearby or in combat with you.

recommendedSettings.value: On if you feel motion sick, otherwise optional
recommendedSettings.why: The game says it may help with motion sickness.

items.notes: Leonida Notebook captured these rows first-hand on an Xbox Series S. Cops no longer appear on the radar automatically (Red Bull), so use Focus to spot them. Drills and goal are coaching suggestions built on the sourced mechanics, not taken from a guide.

items.summary: There is no Performance mode: the game targets 30fps on every console, so calibrate brightness, cut motion blur and use VRR if your TV has it.
instructions: Know the limit: there is no Performance/Quality toggle; GTA VI targets 30fps on Series X, Series S, PS5 and PS5 Pro.
Digital Foundry: Series X can dip into the 20s in heavy chaos; Series S drops more.
Xbox can output a 120Hz signal with VRR at system level, which smooths dropped frames. Turn it on in the Xbox's TV & display options if your TV supports it.
In Settings > Display, run Brightness Calibration and set it so the symbol is barely visible.
Lower Motion Blur Strength (default 3) to Off or 1 for a clearer image when turning.
Set Flashbang to Dark and turn on Brightness Reduction if bright flashes bother you.
Player Status, Hit and Awareness Effects Intensity (default 5) control screen-edge effects; Awareness Effects warn of cops and off-screen threats, so keep that one up.
Safe Zone fits the HUD to your TV's edges.

drills.name: Calibration check
drills.setup: Display tab, then a night drive in Vice City.
drills.howTo: Calibrate brightness, then drive at night; if you cannot see into shadowed alleys, raise it one step.

drills.name: Blur A/B
drills.setup: Any fast drive.
drills.howTo: One lap with Motion Blur Strength 3, one with 0-1; keep whichever lets you read traffic better.

items.goal: Brightness calibrated (symbol barely visible), Motion Blur Strength at 1 or Off, and VRR/120Hz on at console level if your TV supports it.

recommendedSettings.why: games.gg's guidance for correct shadow detail.
Clearer image when panning at 30fps (games.gg).
These screen-edge effects warn of cops and off-screen threats.

recommendedSettings.setting: Xbox console: 120Hz refresh + variable refresh rate
recommendedSettings.value: On, if your TV supports it
recommendedSettings.why: Digital Foundry: VRR in a 120Hz container smooths frame drops on Xbox.

items.notes: The Xbox menu settings are console settings, not GTA VI settings. Frame-rate figures are from Digital Foundry's launch testing and may change with patches. Drills and goal are coaching suggestions built on the sourced mechanics, not taken from a guide.

items.summary: Turn dialogue up, decide on GPS Voice, and use Mono Audio or Tinnitus Reduction if needed.
instructions: Open Settings > Audio.
Separate sliders: Master Volume, Dialogue, Music, SFX, UI and Media.
GPS Voice gives spoken directions (default Off).
Mono Audio puts the same sound in both channels; Tinnitus Reduction cuts the ringing after explosions.
Screen Narration and Audio Descriptions (English only) read menus and describe cutscenes.
Radio: hold D-pad Left to scroll stations; headphones from electronics stores let you listen on foot.

drills.howTo: Close your eyes as a police car passes and point to where it is; adjust SFX vs Music until you can.

drills.howTo: Drive there with GPS Voice on and the minimap set to Dynamic to learn to navigate by ear.

items.goal: With your settings, name the direction of an approaching siren correctly 4 times out of 5 without looking.

recommendedSettings.why: Mission instructions and partner calls are easier to hear.
Leaves room for siren and gunfire cues.
Less ringing after blasts.
Spoken directions let you keep your eyes on the road.

items.summary: Set movement speed and helpers like Auto Equip Helmet and Tap Assist; leave the difficulty-lowering options off if you want to get good.
instructions: Settings > Gameplay > Movement: Movement Speed (default Walk), Combat Movement Speed (default Fast Walk) and Stand & Sprint (Off/On).
Accessibility group: Tap Assist (one press counts as 2x, 3x, 4x, or becomes a hold), Hold Delay, Hold Assist.
Aiming and Interact can be Hold (default) or Press; Loadout and Directional Button Actions can be Hold or Hold & Release.
Nitrous can be Hold or Press (click Left Stick once instead of holding).
Auto Equip Helmet puts a helmet on for you on motorcycles and bikes; helmets cut crash damage (Polygon).
Simplified Mini Games simplifies exercising, hotwiring and basketball inputs.
Accessible Combat (lower enemy health and damage taken) and Reduced Vehicle Damage both 'significantly change the balance'; there is no difficulty setting otherwise.
Auto Drive (Restricted/Unrestricted) drives you to a waypoint in the Cinematic camera.

drills.name: Movement speed feel test
drills.setup: A busy street.
drills.howTo: Try Movement Speed Walk vs Jog (G2A) and keep the one that gets you around without bumping NPCs.

drills.name: Helmet check
drills.setup: Any motorcycle.
drills.howTo: Turn on Auto Equip Helmet and confirm the helmet goes on and off as you mount and leave the bike.

items.summary: Cars are heavy: brake in a straight line before corners, use LT-drift and the A handbrake for tight turns, and Focus for traffic.
instructions: RT accelerates, LT brakes/reverses, A is the handbrake, click Left Stick for horn/nitrous.
Brake before you turn, wheels straight. Braking mid-turn makes the front tyres lose grip and the car slides wide.
Drift: start turning, hold LT, and as the back swings out, steer the other way and get on the gas.
Sharp turn: at high speed hold A while steering to whip round a tight corner or make a fast U-turn.
Click both sticks (Focus) to slow time; it makes heavy traffic or a 90-degree turn at speed far easier.
Duck with B while being shot at in a car.
Some bridges rise for boats: stop and wait for the road to come down.
Dying in a crash keeps banked cash and owned weapons but loses pocket cash.

items.summary: Free aim with Partial assist: hold LT, shoot with RT, read the hit marker colour, and train at the Rodgers Ranch ranges.
instructions: Hold LT to aim and RT to shoot. Aiming is free; assist only nudges and slows the reticle.
Hit markers: white = hit but still fighting, yellow = incapacitated, red = killed.
Limb shots (legs, shoulders) give a yellow, non-lethal result; head and torso kill.
Each gun has damage, accuracy, handling and range ratings; check them before you pick a favourite.
Pay the $5 Waiver Pass at Rodgers Ranch & Shooting Range (north-east Port Gellhorn) or Griffin Shooting Range (Balsero). Three ranges are open at first; playing one unlocks a linked range.
On points ranges, hit a target's body once or twice before the head to build the multiplier; a miss lowers it.
Every time you finish or quit a range class, your Focus stat goes up permanently.
Range medals unlock cheats: 25 Bronze = Max Ammo, 25 Silver = Infinite Ammo, 25 Gold = No Reload.

items.summary: Snap to cover with RB, peek and shoot, suppress with near misses, and heal with Zombix from the loadout.
instructions: Press RB beside solid cover to enter it; press RB again to leave.
At a corner, press A to move round it. Aim with LT to pop out, RT to shoot.
Switch Shoulder swaps the camera side while aiming (GameMeta lists D-pad Left; check the Aiming diagram on the Control Scheme tab).
Near-miss fire suppresses some enemies, including police, buying time to move.
Cover Selection (Gameplay > Combat) decides whether camera facing or movement picks the cover.
Heal: hold LB (loadout) and press X to use Zombix. Carry up to 5; $15 a bottle at convenience stores. It heals more the lower your health is.
Body Armor from Ammu-Nation absorbs damage until it breaks.
Health regenerates slowly only up to a threshold; food, drinks and sleep also heal.

items.summary: Click both sticks while aiming to slow time and show red (lethal) and yellow (non-lethal) weak points on people and vehicles.
instructions: While aiming a firearm, click both sticks (LS + RS) to enter Combat Focus.
Time slows; people show red (lethal) and yellow (non-lethal) weak points.
Vehicles show weak parts too: engine, fuel tank, tyres; a helicopter's tail rotor is the guides' example.
Focus drains the purple bar (top left) in combat. It refills over time; a cigarette refills it out of combat.
Your Criminal Profile decides how it refills in a fight: non-lethal takedowns for Professional/Hardened, headshots for Violent/Psycho.
Out of combat, Focus does not drain and highlights loot (cash, Zombix), interactables, events and police positions.
Focus-marked food and drinks, and washing your face, give a temporary boost.
The Focus stat (how long slow-motion lasts) rises at shooting ranges and other activities; see Character stats.

items.summary: Tap LB to holster, hold LB for the loadout wheel; carry two sidearms and two longarms and store the rest in your trunk or an Ammu-Nation locker.
instructions: Tap LB to holster; hold LB to open the loadout wheel (sidearm slots top right, longarm slot bottom left, plus melee, explosives and items).
Carry up to two sidearms and two longarms. Sidearms hide; one longarm goes on your back, the other in your off hand.
Longarms stay visible and can get you reported; store them before walking into crowds.
Store extras in your personal vehicle's trunk or an Ammu-Nation weapon locker (shared storage). Not every Ammu-Nation has a locker.
To swap: open the trunk or locker, hold LB, highlight a slot and cycle with LT/RT.
Dropped guns are grey (unowned) and lost when you leave them; unique variants (yellow) are added permanently for both characters.
Stand over a dropped gun and hold LB to compare stats (green/red arrows).
Zombix and the Metal Detector live on the wheel too; it flips to a clothing/items wheel (e.g. masks).

items.summary: Crouch with B, tag guards with D-pad Right while aiming, grab from behind with RT and tap X to knock them out.
instructions: Crouch with B to cut visibility and noise; move slowly.
Scout first: click both sticks for Focus to highlight enemies, show where a noise came from and colour doors (white = usable, red = alarmed).
Tag: aim at a guard (gun or binoculars) and press D-pad Right; the tag stays on them and on the minimap.
Takedown: get behind an unaware guard, hold RT to grab, tap X to knock them out. It fails if they turn or see you.
Knocked-out guards can wake up; don't leave one next to a dropped gun, and move bodies out of sight.
There are no vision cones; a yellow bar over an enemy and yellow screen-edge flashes mean you are about to be spotted.
Distract: pick up a bottle and throw it with RT; the guard goes to check the noise.
Buy suppressors at Ammu-Nation for guns you own (not unique weapons). The Assassin Nipper .38 has a built-in silencer.

items.summary: Break line of sight, leave the red search zone, then clear each heat icon (face, outfit, car, gun, partner, CCTV).
instructions: Stars (top right) show how hard police search: 1 star = one car, 2 = several, 3 adds an armed helicopter, up to 6 stars.
Star colours: transparent = crime reported, suspect unknown; white = you are seen; flashing = they are losing you; grey = lost sight; red = wanted in the search zone.
Open the map for the red search area. Lose sight first: fast car, then off-road, swap cars, dive underwater, or enter a building or forest.
Avoid killing cops or civilians; that raises stars and widens the zone. Limb shots incapacitate without killing.

Then clear heat icons: head = cap/sunglasses or haircut; hanger = change clothes; car = Pay 'n' Spray or swap; gun = holster or stow longarms; two heads = split up; camera = destroy the CCTV recorder (not possible if it shows a cloud).
Leave the search zone; the stars fade with time.
Better still: no witnesses, no report. Put a mask on before a crime; witnesses can be slapped to stop a call.
In aircraft, fly low: the ceiling is lower than in GTA V and flying low lowers your chance of being spotted.

items.summary: RT for throttle, pull the left stick back to climb (inverted by default), X/B for the rudder, LT to slow for landing.
instructions: No flight school or licence: get in and fly. Helicopters take a few seconds to spin up.
Planes: hold RT for throttle, then pull the left stick back to lift off. Pitch is inverted by default.
Rudder (yaw) is X and B on Xbox, not the bumpers as in GTA V.
Helicopters: RT climbs, LT descends, same yaw buttons.
Landing: line up early, use the rudder for small corrections, let off the throttle and hold LT, come in shallow. Click Left Stick for the landing gear.
Turn Aircraft Movement off (Controller > Inverted Controls) if you want up to climb; turn Follow Roll off (Camera) for a steadier horizon.
Map-marked airfields and helipads spawn free aircraft with no wanted level; the airport and Mile Zero Air Station give you stars.
The flight ceiling is low; an alarm sounds and a red line appears when you hit it.

instructions: Free boats: Jason's own boat at the dock behind his house in the Keys, and Kenton's boat beside Island Dreams Boat Charters in Key Lento.
RT throttle, LT slow/reverse, hold A while steering for a sharper turn.

items.summary: Each character has Strength (health), Cardio (stamina) and Focus (slow-time), max Level 4; train both characters, ideally together.
instructions: Strength raises max health. Train with the weights on Jason's terrace (from Chapter 1) or buy a gym membership (a few hundred dollars).
Cardio raises max stamina: treadmill and exercise bike are quickest; running, cycling, swimming and kayaking count.
Workout Windows: each exercise gives about 11%, up to 33% a day, so about 3 windows per level. A window reopens after about a day (half a day with a protein bar or shake).
Finish the workout to keep the gains; a set ends early if stamina runs out. Strength and Cardio drop if you stop training.
Focus has no windows: shooting ranges (every finished or quit class), fishing, pool, mini-golf, golf putting and meditation raise it.
Stats are per character. If your partner is with you at the gym, they work out too.
Check stats in the pause menu under Jason & Lucia, or in the phone's Fitness app.
Insider Gaming (via FullBoosts): Jason starts with decent Strength but weak Cardio and Focus.

items.summary: Both share Focus and the same stats; they differ in melee style. Switch with D-pad Right then RB once Chapter 2 unlocks it.
instructions: Both have Focus and the same three stats, tracked separately per character.
Melee differs: Jason is a heavy-hitting street brawler; Lucia is a technical, agile kickboxer.
Free switching unlocks mid-Chapter 2 (Polygon: after Breakfast Run; Red Bull: Coffee Break): hold D-pad Right, then pick the other portrait (RB). Some missions lock you to one character.
The same partner menu (D-pad Right) lets you summon your partner or split up.
Together you carry two loot bags in robberies, and one can drive while the other shoots.
Split up after a crime to clear the partner heat icon.
When together, activity and Criminal Profile gains are shared, and gym sessions train both.
The relationship has four levels (Running on Empty, Partners in Crime, Crazy in Love, Hot Together), raised by kind acts and shared activities.

items.summary: D-pad Up opens the phone (hold for WAiNK); BuckMe is your bank; hold D-pad Down for quick navigation.
instructions: Press D-pad Up for the phone; hold D-pad Up to jump straight to WAiNK.
WAiNK scans parked cars: lock, alarm, tracker, value, registration cost.
BuckMe (after the Buck Me! mission) is your bank: balance, transactions and the ATM Finder. You can pay for most services with it.
Scooter Bros (Chapter 2, Moses) delivers your personal vehicle, trunk weapons included, for a fee; it can also return impounded cars.
RydeMe books taxis and fast travel; Vice City Real Estate buys garages.
Fitness shows Strength, Cardio, Focus and nutrition; WhatUp holds mission messages; Weather helps plan flights.
Hold D-pad Down for objective, minimap and quick navigation to a nearby place without opening the map.
View opens the map.

items.summary: Bank cash often (pocket cash is lost on death and at risk on arrest), go straight for the register and safe, and leave before the cops arrive.
instructions: Pocket cash is lost when you die (Wasted) and at risk when Busted; banked cash and owned weapons are kept.
Stash cash under Jason's bedroom floorboard early, then deposit at ATMs once unlocked (BuckMe ATM Finder).
GTA6.house gives a $20,000 pocket-cash cap and a $15,000 BuckMe checking limit.
Robbing civilians pays a few dollars; in stores, go straight for the register, then the safe (the cashier may give you the code).
Speed matters: when you hear sirens, stop looting and escape. Losing everything is worse than leaving loot.
Rob with your partner to carry two bags.
Use Scooter Bros instead of stealing back an impounded car (a few hundred dollars).
See the Steal tab for payouts by activity.
